newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-TRAPATTONI STAYING AT BAYERN MUNICH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TRAPATTONI STAYING AT BAYERN MUNICH.

text.p: Giovanni Trapattoni confirmed on Monday that he will remain Bayern Munich coach next season after the German club refused to let him join Roma.
Trapattoni had been linked to the Italian serie A club, who fired Argentine Carlos Bianchi earlier in the season and appointed 74-year-old Swede Nils Liedholm as a stopgap.
But the Italian told state RAI television that Bayern had refused to allow him to terminate his contract with the Bundesliga leaders a season early.
"I met president (Franco) Sensi a week ago and we agreed that if I could get the go-ahead from Bayern I would coach Roma," said Trapattoni.
"It did not work out that way because Bayern, a club that I am obliged to because they took me at a difficult moment, refused to relinquish my contract.,"

Trapattoni, the most successful coach in Italiy who led both Juventus and Internazionale to a total of eight titles, said he had never signed anything with Roma but had agreed a conditional verbal undertaking.
"Now I have nothing more to add," he said. "Its too early to say what I'll do when my contract with Bayern expires. I prefer to live from day to day."
Roma must now find a new coach at a point in the season when many clubs have already lined up their management team for the coming year.

But the list of favourites is sure to include Fiorentina's Claudio Ranieri, a former Roma player who comes from the capital. His team have had a disappointing season after winning the Italian Cup last year.
Others might be AC Milan's Arrigo Sacchi, likely to make way for a returning Fabio Capello, and Zdenek Zeman, who is currently without a club after being fired by Lazio.
